# Angular Anything

> Move a React, Vue or AngularJS app or library to modern Angular with agents, and prove it still behaves the same. The tool records the original in Chromium and fails the Angular port on any difference it compares. It does not write the port: your agent does.

Status: early. Tested on macOS only. Read https://github.com/erkamyaman/angular-anything/blob/main/docs/reference.md before relying on it.

Loading and pending UI is never compared (a spinner, a "Loading..." text, a button that is disabled while saving). A request is answered before a step is observed, so a port without that UI passes. Compare it with the original by reading its code.

## Install

Needs Node 24 or newer.

    npm install -g angular-anything
    angular-anything doctor

If `doctor` says Chromium is missing, run the command it prints.

In the commands below, `aa` stands for `angular-anything`. Run it from the folder that holds `cases/`.

## Set up the port

The port is a normal Angular project made with the Angular CLI (`ng new`). The tool is tested with Angular 22. One layout that works, with every `aa` command run from `port/`:

    original/                    the app as it is
    port/                        the Angular project
      src/
      cases/<suite>/<id>/case.json
      recordings/<source>/       written by record
      reports/<source>/          written by gate, replay and drift

- Angular removes white space between elements by default. Where the original has white space that the browser renders, for example between two inline elements or on two lines of a form, set `preserveWhitespaces: true` on the component and keep that space in the template.
- The gate compares attributes, also the `_ngcontent-*` ones of emulated view encapsulation. Give a component with styles `ViewEncapsulation.None`, or keep its styles in a global stylesheet.

## Commands

    aa doctor
    aa record <suite> --source <name> --url <original-url>
    aa gate <suite> --source <name> --url <port-url> [--original-url <original-url>]
    aa replay <suite> --source <name> --url <port-url>
    aa drift <suite> --source <name> --url <port-url> --original-url <original-url>

- `doctor` checks Node, Playwright and Chromium.
- `record` runs each case twice against the original and writes `recordings/<source>`.
- `gate` checks the lock, replays every case against the port and writes `reports/<source>`.
- `replay` is `gate` without the lock check.
- `drift` says whether the original changed or the port regressed.
- `--original-url` also compares sizes, positions and screenshots (screenshots never fail the gate).
- `--redact` (`replay`, `gate`) writes shapes only, no values.
- `--original-source <dir> --port-source <dir>` (`gate`) fails a port that holds recorded values the original source does not hold. In the layout above: `--original-source ../original --port-source src`. The port source folder must not hold `recordings/` or `cases/`, or their own files fail the check, so do not give the root of the project. The original source folder must not hold the port source or `recordings/`, or lie inside `recordings/`.

`record` and `gate` take a while: in one trial 24 cases took about 2.5 minutes to record and 2 minutes to gate. There is no option that runs a single case, so run both with a long timeout.

Exit codes of `gate` and `replay`: 0 everything matches, 1 mismatch or refused recording, 2 wrong command line.

## A case

`cases/<suite>/<id>/case.json`:

    {
      "format": "angular-anything/case@1",
      "id": "add-task",
      "description": "Add a task",
      "viewport": { "width": 1024, "height": 768 },
      "steps": [
        { "action": "goto", "path": "/" },
        { "action": "fill", "target": { "role": "textbox", "name": "New task" }, "value": "Call mom" },
        { "action": "click", "target": { "role": "button", "name": "Add" } },
        { "action": "press", "target": { "role": "textbox", "name": "New task" }, "key": "Enter" },
        { "action": "advance", "frames": 125 }
      ]
    }

Actions: `goto`, `click`, `dblclick`, `hover`, `check`, `uncheck`, `fill`, `press`, `reload`, `advance`. Targets are found by accessibility role and name, with `index` and `within` when more than one matches. The clock of the page is paused and moves only with `advance` (one frame is 16 ms).

## Backend state and error states

`record` sends the requests of the first run of each case to the real backend, writes included, and resets nothing. What one case writes is still there in the next case and in the next `record`. The second run of a case gets its `fetch` and XHR answers from the first.

- Give the test backend a reset address and visit it before the app: `{ "action": "goto", "path": "/api/reset" }` as step 1, then `{ "action": "goto", "path": "/" }`. A `goto` is a page load that is not answered from the recording, in `record` and in `gate`. It must answer with a status below 400 and its page is compared like any step, so the server of the port has to answer that path as the original's does (for example by passing it on to the test backend).
- The tool cannot fake an answer. To record an error state the test backend must return the error, so it needs a switch, for example `{ "action": "goto", "path": "/api/test/fail?method=POST" }` after the reset. The reset has to turn the switch off again.

Both addresses are ones you build into a test backend. Never add them to a production one.

## Write the port the Angular way

The gate checks behaviour only, not code quality. While writing the port, follow Angular's own guidance:

- Style guide: https://angular.dev/style-guide
- Agent skills from the Angular team, `angular-developer` and `angular-new-app`: https://github.com/angular/skills (install with `npx skills add https://github.com/angular/skills`, ask the user first)
- The MCP server of the Angular CLI, `ng mcp`, for documentation and best practices that match the project's version: https://angular.dev/ai/mcp
- The latest Angular the tool is tested with (22): standalone components, signals, signal inputs and `@if`/`@for`.

Where Angular guidance and the original's behaviour or markup conflict, keep the behaviour: the gate decides. Tell the user where that happened.

## Porting workflow

1. Start the original app and its backend with test data. `record` sends real requests to it, writes included, and does not reset it (see "Backend state and error states").
2. Write the cases yourself, do not wait for the user to describe them. Read the routes, forms, buttons and requests in the code, use the running app, and write one case per thing a user can do, including empty, error and reload states. Start small, then tell the user which flows are covered and which are not.
3. Run `aa record`. If it refuses (the two runs differ, a secret is found, the page does something the tape cannot hold), read the message and the reference. Do not remove a check to make it pass.
4. Port the app to Angular (see "Write the port the Angular way"). Mount each component on an element the original already has, so that no wrapper element or extra attribute appears (reference, "Choosing the selector of a component in the Angular port").
5. Start the port and run `aa gate` with `--original-source` and `--port-source`. Fix the port, not the recording, until it exits 0.
6. Run `aa gate` again, with `--original-url` added, while the original still runs.
7. After any cleanup of the port's code, run both gates again.

## Rules for agents

- Never edit anything under `recordings/` by hand.
- Never copy recorded values into the port to make the gate pass.
- Ask the user before adding a mask or noise entry: it makes the gate check less.
- Do not record against production data or with real secrets.
